title: Dangote Appoints Zedcrest Securities as IPO Broker: What It Means for Nigerian Investors
summary: Dangote Group has appointed Zedcrest Securities as a Joint Stockbroker on the Dangote Refinery IPO. Here is what the appointment means, who Zedcrest is, and what every Nigerian investor should do right now.
body_markdown:
When a company begins appointing stockbrokers to an IPO, it is not housekeeping. It is a sign that the machinery of a public offering is fully engaged and the subscription window is close.


On June 22, 2026,[Business Day reported](https://businessday.ng/news/article/dangote-appoints-zedcrest-securities-as-ipo-broker-as-listing-nears/) that the Dangote Group has appointed Zedcrest Securities as a Joint Stockbroker on the proposed Initial Public Offering of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery. The appointment places Zedcrest alongside the previously announced advisory and distribution team for what is expected to be the largest equity capital market transaction in Nigerian history and the largest IPO on any African exchange.


The article also confirmed an operational update worth noting: the refinery is now running at 700,000 barrels per day, an increase from the 650,000-barrel nameplate capacity that has been the reference figure in most previous coverage. That upgrade, confirmed by CEO David Bird in March 2026, is now the current operational baseline for the asset behind the IPO.


For Nigerian retail investors who have been following the[Dangote Refinery IPO](https://learn.investbamboo.com/what-happens-if-the-dangote-ipo-is-oversubscribed-understanding-ipo-demand-in-nigeria/) since its announcement, the Zedcrest appointment is a concrete signal of how close the listing has become. This article explains who Zedcrest Securities is, what a joint stockbroker does in a Nigerian IPO, what the full advisory team now looks like, and what every investor should do before the subscription window opens.


---


## Who Is Zedcrest Securities?


Zedcrest Securities is a Nigerian capital market firm with an established track record in fixed income, equities, and institutional securities. The business serves a broad client base that includes institutional investors, corporates, asset managers, pension funds, and foreign portfolio investors operating in the Nigerian market.


The firm significantly expanded its stockbroking capabilities less than two years ago through the[acquisition of RMB Nigeria Stockbrokers](https://businessday.ng/news/article/dangote-appoints-zedcrest-securities-as-ipo-broker-as-listing-nears/) , the stockbroking subsidiary of Rand Merchant Bank, the Corporate and Investment Banking arm of FirstRand Group. Following the acquisition, the business was rebranded as Zedcrest Securities as part of a broader strategy to build a full-service capital markets franchise. The acquisition brought institutional market access, established relationships with foreign investors, and enhanced execution capabilities in the Nigerian equities market.


Zedcrest’s appointment on the Dangote Refinery IPO reflects the depth of its institutional relationships, particularly among pension funds and foreign portfolio investors, two investor categories that will constitute significant demand pools for a transaction of this scale. Its experience in executing large, institutional-grade securities transactions makes it a natural fit for the distribution role in Africa’s most closely watched IPO.


---


## What a Joint Stockbroker Does in a Nigerian IPO


The term “Joint Stockbroker” is specific to the Nigerian primary market. Understanding what the role involves clarifies why the appointment matters and how it affects the distribution of shares to different investor categories.


In a Nigerian IPO, the issuing company appoints a team of market operators to manage different aspects of the distribution process. The issuing houses, which in this case include Stanbic IBTC Capital, Vetiva Advisory Services, and FirstCap, are responsible for the overall structuring, regulatory filing, and investor roadshow for the transaction. The stockbrokers operate alongside the issuing houses with a distinct but complementary function: they are responsible for receiving applications from investors, matching supply with demand within their designated investor pools, and coordinating the allotment process with the registrar.


A Joint Stockbroker is one of several brokers appointed to share this distribution function across different investor segments. The appointment of multiple joint stockbrokers is standard practice for large Nigerian public offerings because it broadens the reach of the distribution infrastructure: each broker brings its own client base, its own institutional relationships, and its own operational capacity to process applications.


For the Dangote Refinery IPO, the division of distribution responsibilities across the advisory team means that institutional investors, pension funds, foreign portfolio investors, and retail investors will each have designated access routes to the offering. Zedcrest’s appointment reinforces the institutional and foreign investor access channels, which complements the retail distribution capabilities provided by platforms like[Bamboo](https://investbamboo.com/) .


---


## The Full Advisory and Distribution Team


With the Zedcrest appointment, the known advisory and distribution infrastructure for the Dangote Refinery IPO now includes:


**Stanbic IBTC Capital:** Managing international institutional placement, responsible for connecting the transaction with foreign asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, and international institutional investors who want exposure to the Nigerian energy sector.


**Vetiva Advisory Services:** Managing local market distribution, responsible for coordinating the retail and domestic institutional subscription process in Nigeria.


**FirstCap:** Focused on Nigerian institutional investors, primarily pension funds and domestic asset managers whose allocations will constitute a structural anchor of demand in the offering.


**Zedcrest Securities (newly appointed):** A Joint Stockbroker role that reinforces institutional distribution capacity, particularly for the pension fund and foreign investor channels given the firm’s client base.


This is the most complete picture of the distribution team that has been publicly confirmed. The breadth of the team signals that the Dangote Group has assembled execution capacity across every major investor category: retail, domestic institutional, pension fund, and international. Each layer of the distribution infrastructure is now in place.


The transaction is no longer in the planning phase. It is in the execution phase.


---


## The 700,000 Barrels Per Day Update


The Business Day article references the refinery as a “now 700,000-barrel-per-day” facility. This is an important operational update that changes the reference figure used in describing the asset throughout the IPO coverage.


Earlier in 2026, the refinery’s nameplate capacity was described as 650,000 barrels per day, the figure confirmed at commissioning. In March 2026, CEO David Bird confirmed that the refinery had completed a performance test run at 661,000 barrels per day and that the near-term target was 700,000 barrels per day, pending insurance and market stakeholder approvals. The Business Day confirmation, published June 22, suggests that target has now been achieved or is being treated as the operational standard.


At 700,000 barrels per day, the Dangote Refinery processes more crude oil daily than any other single-train refinery in the world. It also processes approximately 50,000 more barrels per day than the figure that underpinned earlier valuation estimates. That operational improvement has a direct implication for earnings projections: more throughput at a stable crack spread produces more revenue and more margin. Investors who have been working with 650,000 bpd as their throughput assumption should update their mental model of the asset.


For context, the valuation range of $40 billion to $50 billion that has been cited throughout the IPO coverage was derived at a time when the refinery was ramping toward nameplate capacity. A refinery now operating above that nameplate capacity, and confirmed at 700,000 bpd by external media, is a materially stronger asset than the one described in the earliest coverage.


---


## What the Appointment Signals About the IPO Timeline


Every development in the lead-up to a major IPO follows a sequence. The appointment of financial advisers is early-stage. The filing of the prospectus with the SEC is mid-stage. The appointment and activation of stockbrokers marks the late-stage, distribution-ready phase. It is the preparation immediately preceding the opening of a subscription window.


The Dangote Refinery prospectus was submitted to the[Securities and Exchange Commission](https://sec.gov.ng/) for review in April 2026. The SEC review process for a transaction of this complexity is expected to take several weeks. Investor roadshows were announced for the period following SEC approval. The subscription window has been publicly indicated for August 2026.


The Zedcrest appointment, published June 22, 2026, is consistent with a timeline in which the subscription window opens in August. Stockbrokers are not appointed months in advance of an offer opening. They are appointed in the weeks or months immediately preceding it, once the offer structure is confirmed and the distribution logistics need to be finalised.


Nigerian investors who have been following this transaction with the intention of participating should treat the Zedcrest appointment as a timeline signal: the window to prepare is narrowing, not widening. If your[Bamboo](https://investbamboo.com/) account is not yet open, your[CSCS account](https://learn.investbamboo.com/what-is-an-ipo-a-complete-guide-for-nigerian-investors/) is not confirmed, and your capital is not positioned, the Zedcrest news is a prompt to act now.


---


## What This Means for Retail Investors


Several things the Zedcrest appointment confirms are directly relevant to retail investors approaching the offer.


### Retail Access Runs Through Licensed Platforms and Brokers


The joint stockbroker structure confirms that retail investors access this IPO through licensed brokers and investment platforms, not through direct applications to Dangote Group or through any unofficial channel. Zedcrest, Vetiva, and the other members of the distribution team are the licensed entities through which applications flow to the registrar.


[Bamboo](https://investbamboo.com/) operates within this framework as a licensed SEC-registered digital sub-broker. When the subscription window opens on Bamboo, applications submitted through the platform are routed through the official distribution infrastructure to the registrar, using your verified account details and confirmed CSCS number. The process is the same whether you apply through Bamboo or through a traditional licensed stockbroker. The difference is that Bamboo handles the paperwork on your behalf, removes the manual form-filling, and processes refunds directly to your wallet.


### The Dollar Dividend Commitment Remains in Place


The Business Day article reconfirms Aliko Dangote’s assurance that shareholders will receive returns in dollars despite purchasing shares in naira. This is the most recent public reaffirmation of the dollar dividend commitment, published June 22, 2026. The arrangement remains subject to final SEC and CBN approval and will be confirmed in the prospectus, but the continued public restatement of the commitment at this late stage of the IPO process is a positive signal for investors for whom the dollar income structure is a key part of the investment case.


### The Institutional Infrastructure Strengthens the Offer


The breadth of the distribution team, now including Zedcrest’s institutional and foreign investor network, is significant for retail investors because it strengthens the structural demand floor beneath the offering. An IPO with strong institutional demand is less likely to be undersubscribed and more likely to list with meaningful price support from institutional holders who have conviction positions. Zedcrest’s appointment adds foreign portfolio investor demand to the mix, which also matters for long-term price stability: foreign institutional investors who hold positions through an IPO typically stay invested for longer periods than short-term retail traders, which improves post-listing liquidity depth.

**Open your Bamboo account if you have not already.** Visit[investbamboo.com](https://investbamboo.com/) or[download the Bamboo app](https://onelink.to/investbamboo) . Account verification takes a few business days. Do not leave this for July.


**Confirm your CSCS number.** Your CSCS number is the unique identifier through which the registrar credits allotted shares to your account. It is in your Bamboo profile once your Nigerian stocks access is activated. An incorrect or missing CSCS number invalidates your application. Confirm it now.


**Fund your account above your target investment.** In an oversubscribed offer, applying for more than your target allocation is the most effective strategy for receiving close to your intended position size. Your application must be fully funded. Fund your wallet in advance, not on the day the subscription window opens.


**Read the prospectus when it is published.** The approved prospectus will be available through the NGX website, the SEC Nigeria portal, and through the Bamboo app once the offer goes live. The firm was created following the acquisition of RMB Nigeria Stockbrokers, the stockbroking subsidiary of Rand Merchant Bank. As a Joint Stockbroker, Zedcrest is responsible for receiving and processing investor applications and coordinating with the registrar on allotment, with a particular focus on institutional and foreign portfolio investors.


**What does the Zedcrest appointment mean for the IPO timeline?** Stockbroker appointments are made in the final phase of IPO preparation, once the offer structure is confirmed and distribution logistics are being finalised. It signals that the transaction is in the execution phase, not the planning phase.


**Is the Dangote Refinery still targeting 700,000 barrels per day?** Yes.
